COVID: Testing in South Africa

By: Julian Sun | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
With local transmission of COVID-19 now occurring, does South Africa have the ability to mass test it's population?

Unique Selling Point:
We breakdown South Africa's ability to test for COVID-19, which is essential to flatten the curve of infection.

Summary:
As the COVID-19 pandemic sweeps the globe, it is clear that the countries that have the most effective testing have been the ones to have recorded the fewest deaths, as well as seemingly getting the spread of the virus under control. We look at the what has been achieved in South Korea (vigorous testing of the population has controlled the spread) & Germany (fewer deaths compared with the rest of Europe) as examples. Those countries which have failed to test effectively such as Italy (which allowed the virus to spread unchecked in Bergamo) and the United States (https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2020/mar/28/trump-coronavirus-politics-us-health-disaster?CMP=Share_iOSApp_Other) are being overwhelmed by the rate of infection.



Further information:
Here in South Africa, how are our testing capabilities measuring up? Even though there are over 1000 infections, we have only 2 recorded deaths at this stage. In this story we will look at how the NICD has tested for the virus since it’s inception. How does a test work? How many people have they tested? Who has been carrying out these tests?

With the virus well and truly on our shores and spreading rapidly, how does the rate of testing ramp up? Are we capable of mass testing the South African population? Last night President Ramaphosa announced a major new screening and testing initiative. This is a very important part my story, we’d like to focus on this. Please can you let me know how the NICD will be involved with this?

We will look at the government’s partnership with private labs like Lancet who are the main testing agency being used. How many labs around the country are carrying out COVID-19 tests? How many tests can be carried out in a day? How many testing kits do we have before we run out? How long does it take to get results?

We will also look at the cost of these tests. Does medical aid pay for these tests? How much does it cost if you don’t have medical aid? A test at Lancet costs around R1600. https://www.channel24.co.za/The-Juice/News/somizi-tests-for-covid-19-and-speaks-out-about-the-price-of-test-kits-in-sa-20200318 Why does it cost so much? Gift of the Givers are rolling out drive though test facilities which cost R750. Why the price discrepancy?

Overseas several private hospitals have been accused of trying to make a profit from testing. Is this the case here? https://www.google.co.za/amp/s/ahvalnews.com/turkey-coronavirus/turkish-private-hospitals-profit-covid-19-tests-hurriyet%3famp

Prof. Shabir Madhi
Dr. Kamy Chetty

Press Release:


Well into South Africa’s stringent 21-day national lockdown and with government on high alert, the number of positive patients is still steadily rising and with a delay in obtaining results, it seems the country’s infection rate may be skewed. Countries that have seemed to get on top of the COVID-19 pandemic appear to have rolled out testing to the highest number of people. Now the national Health Department has set out an ambitious plan to screen and test thousands in every province. So could an intensified roll-out of screening and testing finally be the difference?

Script:


INTRO V/O: The UN calls COVID-19 “the greatest crisis facing humanity since the Second World War”

With the global death toll now over 100 000, many countries like Italy, Spain and the United States are being overwhelmed by the sheer scale of the pandemic.

On the other hand those that carried out early and extensive tests for the disease (like South Korea), have been able to flatten the curve of infection.

Here in South Africa the government is in a race against time to control the spread of the virus.

Ramaphosa up-sound

V/O: What happens next will determine the fate of millions.



OPENING LINK: Last week the world passed the grim milestone of 1 million confirmed cases of COVID-19. As this global pandemic continues to rage, South Africa is at a crossroads and winning the battle will hinge on how quickly and how broadly we begin to test for the virus.

V/O: Professor Shabir Madhi, a virologist at WITS University sees lessons that can be learnt from South Korea

South Korea had a strategy in place that relied on early screening and testing of its population

V/O: South Korea conducted hundreds of thousands of tests early and was able to limit the number of cases to around 10 000 and just over 200 deaths

In stark contrast, the United States was slow to begin testing. There are now half a million infected and a projected death toll in the tens (if not hundreds) of thousands.

Prof Madhi on the failure of the US to test

V/O: With South Africa in lockdown, figures here are still low with around 2000 infections and a relatively small death toll.

But Health Minister Zweli Mkhize has warned against complacency

Zweli Mhize: “We may be experiencing the calm before a heavy and devastating storm”

Prof Madhi on the need to test extensively or we’re blind to the problem

V/O: This is because South Africa has carried out just over 60 000 tests in the country so far, spearheaded by the NHLS. Dr Kamy Chetty is their CEO

On why so few tests have been carried out to date

On ramping up to 5000 tests per day.

On not getting enough samples to carry out 5000 a day

V/O: The majority of South African labs (both public and private) use what’s called a PCR Test. While very accurate, it can take several days to get a result. Dr Florette Treurnicht from the NICD explains why

Dr Floret explains what a PCR test is and why it takes 3-4 days for a result

V/O: Right now it is crucial to ramp up the number of tests that can be done per day. That’s why the NHLS is turning to a faster type of PCR technology. It utilizes a machine called a Gene X-pert, (which has been used widely in South Africa to test for TB). The manufacturers have created a COVID-19 test that can give results in just 45 minutes.

Dr Treurnicht on the advantages of Gene X-Pert

Dr Chetty on when Gene X-pert will be rolled out and how it will allow the NHLS to ramp up to 30000 tests per day

V/O: To date the majority of Covid-19 tests have been carried out by private labs like Lancet.

Dr Eftyhia Vardas explains how they’ve struggled to cope with the demand.

On the number of tests that Lancet have had to carry out

On struggling to cope with demand, leading to 5days to get a result but now they’ve got it under control

V/O: To ease the pressure on Private labs, Gift of the Givers have set up several testing sites around the country, explains Dr Imtiaz Sooliman

On why they set up the labs

V/O: While infection numbers are still relatively low, government is worried about the scale of local transmission that’s occurring in high density areas. which is why they’ve launched a crucial mass screening & testing drive

Dr Chetty & Prof Madhi on the importance of mass testing

LINK 2: This is one of the brand new mobile testing labs that will be deployed around the country. These state of the art vehicles will allow for testing in remote and rural communities. As such they represent the frontline in South Africa’s fight against COVID-19

Dr Chetty on the mobile testing drive

V/O: One major stumbling block in South Africa’s drive to mass test is the global demand for the reagents needed for testing.

Dr Vardas on the lack of reagents and relying on the Minister to negotiate for them
V/O: The government aims to be able to conduct 35000 tests a day by the end of April. Whether it succeeds or not will determine the fate of the country.



PROMO 1: The number of COVID-19 positive cases in South Africa is relatively low compared to the rest of the world. But are our numbers accurate and is this just the calm before the onslaught of a storm that threatens to overwhelm us?

PROMO 2: As the COVID-19 pandemic sweeps the globe, it’s clear that the countries that test the most have the least number of deaths. Now South Africa is set to screen and test thousands across the country in a bid to slow down the virus.

PROMO 3: The WHO has begged countries to “test, test, test” to control the spread of COVID-19. Now thousands of healthcare workers are criss-crossing the country in a desperate bid the flatten the curve.
